Professional practice loan

After this lesson you can:
  • Distinguish practice lending from generic business lending
  • Anchor eligibility on professional registration

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

1. The product

A term loan to a practising professional — doctor, chartered accountant, architect, lawyer — for clinic equipment, premises or working needs. The distinguishing asset is the professional registration: an active licence with a regulator (MCI/NMC, ICAI, bar council) anchors both identity and earning credibility, alongside practice receipts and tax returns.

Risk behaves differently: earning capacity is personal and licence-bound, so registration status is verified at origination and re-verified during the loan's life.

2. What a BA watches

The registration-reverification servicing capability is the tell: a suspended licence is a material change that policy must catch. Practice cash flows can be lumpy (insurance reimbursements, seasonal filings) — schedule design and hardship handling should expect it.

Knowledge check

Answer aloud or write your choice before opening the explanation. If you miss it, revisit the named section—not the whole lesson.

1. Why does this journey re-verify professional registration during servicing?

  1. Marketing data
  2. A lapsed or suspended licence removes the earning basis the loan was sanctioned on
  3. Tax rules
  4. It doesn't
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. The licence is the credit anchor; its loss is a material adverse change the platform must surface.
